payload.goal:
Add order priority and backorders to this warehouse codebase, across every layer that already exists.

Domain  - src/domain/orders.ts:
- Export type OrderPriority = "standard" | "express".
- Order gains a readonly priority field of that type. It is optional at the call site: an order placed without a priority is treated as "standard", so existing callers keep working unchanged.
- placeOrder throws OrderError when a priority is supplied and is neither "standard" nor "express".
- Export interface Backorder with readonly orderId, skuId and missing fields, where missing is a positive integer.
- WarehouseState gains a readonly backorders field keyed by order id.
- reserveOrder records a Backorder for every line whose quantity exceeds the available units, instead of throwing, and leaves the order in a status from which it can still be cancelled.
- Export listBackorders(state) returning every recorded Backorder.

Application  - src/application/warehouse-service.ts:
- The service exposes the new operations and emits a warehouse event for a recorded backorder.

Fulfillment  - src/fulfillment/planner.ts:
- Within one wave, planFulfillment lists express orders before standard ones. Its existing signature does not change.

Durability  - src/durability/journal.ts:
- HistoryAnalytics gains a backorders count derived from the events.

API  - src/api/server.ts:
- The server exposes the backorders of the current state.

Presentation  - src/presentation/tower.ts:
- The rendered SVG distinguishes express orders from standard ones.

Probe  - src/probe/g6.ts and a package script named study:g6-probe:
- Follow the shape of the existing probes: export main() returning a JSON string, and write exactly one JSON object to stdout when invoked directly, with no other output.
- Two invocations from the same commit must emit byte-identical output.

Preserve all existing behaviour and keep every existing test passing. Put new tests next to the code they cover, inside the directories the test script already scans.

scripts.test: node --test src/domain/*.test.ts src/probe/*.test.ts src/scenarios/*.test.ts src/application/*.test.ts src/presentation/*.test.ts src/api/*.test.ts src/fulfillment/*.test.ts src/durability/*.test.ts

root.title: Order priority and backorders across warehouse layers
root.objective: Add order priority, backorders, and deterministic probe support while preserving existing behavior.
expectedOutcomes: Orders accept an optional priority defaulting to standard.
Backorders are recorded and queryable instead of hard-failing reservation flow.
Fulfillment, durability, API, and presentation observe the new order semantics consistently.
The g6 probe follows the existing probe shape and remains deterministic.
Existing tests continue to pass.

complexitySignals.rationale: The change crosses every existing warehouse layer plus a new probe entry point, so the root stays broad while the leaves remain independently testable.

cut.rationale: The work spans multiple already-existing boundaries, so the decomposition follows integration seams that can each be verified with focused tests.

children.title: Domain order semantics
children.objective: Extend orders with priority, backorders, and listBackorders while keeping cancelability and validation intact.
expectedOutcomes: OrderPriority is exported and optional at the call site defaults to standard.
Supplied priorities outside standard or express trigger OrderError.

reserveOrder records backorders for short lines and preserves a cancelable order state.
listBackorders returns the recorded backorders.

children.title: Warehouse service exposure
children.objective: Expose the new operations from the service layer and emit a warehouse event when a backorder is recorded.
expectedOutcomes: The service surface exposes the new backorder-related operation(s).
Recording a backorder emits a warehouse event.
Service tests cover the new behavior without regressing the existing flow.

children.title: Wave fulfillment ordering
children.objective: Keep the existing planner signature and order express work before standard work within a wave.
expectedOutcomes: Within one wave, express orders are planned before standard orders.
The planner signature stays unchanged.
Planner tests pin the new ordering while preserving existing behavior.

children.title: Journal analytics derivation
children.objective: Derive a backorders count in HistoryAnalytics from the recorded events.
expectedOutcomes: HistoryAnalytics includes a backorders count.
The count is derived from journaled events rather than ad hoc state.
Journal tests validate the new derived metric alongside existing analytics.

children.title: API state exposure
children.objective: Expose the current state's backorders through the server surface.
expectedOutcomes: The server returns backorders from the current state.
The response shape is stable enough for current consumers.
API tests cover the exposed backorder data.

children.title: Tower SVG rendering
children.objective: Render express orders distinctly from standard orders in the SVG output.
expectedOutcomes: Express and standard orders are visually distinguishable in the tower SVG.
Existing presentation behavior remains intact apart from the requested distinction.
Presentation tests assert the new visual encoding.

Another probe module exists in the same family, confirming the probe surface is intentionally partitioned.
A third existing probe reinforces the established study-probe pattern to reuse for g6.
